To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the filter width is the crucial parameter in the hybrid RANS/LES modeling and that it has to be determined properly for each particular flow configuration and each particular turbulence model formulation.

the influence of the choice of the filter width on the performance of hybrid turbulence models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the VLES approach is superior to the DES method in the sense that the former is capable of predicting the flow physics in a better manner, especially when the turbulence structures are of a very small size and the grid resolution is relatively low.
the choice of the filter width criterion is not crucial for the overall flow prediction.
the VLES model provides a promising alternative for the hybridization of RANS and LES approaches for the simulation of complex wall-bounded turbulent flows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the filter width is a crucial parameter for VLES modeling and the choice of an appropriate criterion is of utmost importance.
the gridspacing-based filter width is the best choice for the VLES approach, as it yields a good balance between the computational costs and accuracy.
the filter width formulations of Speziale and of Chang are equivalent in the sense that they both lead to the same results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the filter-width formulation has a significant impact on the solution quality.
the grid-spacingbased formulations for the filter-width, which are used in the VLES framework, are not suitable for the application of the hybrid turbulence modeling approach.
the filter width formulation is a very important parameter for hybrid LES/RANS models, which has to be chosen carefully.
